title: One HTML file, 90 portraits and a very patient AI: how Rex Romanorum got made
author: Oador
selftext:
I'm a lawyer by trade, not a programmer. A few months ago I wanted a grand strategy game about the Holy Roman Empire that I couldn't find anywhere, so I started building one with AI. It's now playable, has three campaigns, and is live on [Kickstarter](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/oador/rex-romanorum).

Here's how it came together.



\*\*The whole game is one file\*\*

Rex Romanorum is a single HTML file, about half a megabyte of JavaScript, with d3 drawing the map. No engine, no build step for the web version. That turned out to be a superpower: I can open it anywhere, test it in a browser, and hand the whole thing to the AI in one go when something needs changing.

For the desktop edition, a small Electron wrapper takes the same file, swaps the online fonts and libraries for bundled copies, and unlocks the extra content. One codebase, two editions.

\*\*Design is mine, code is Claude's\*\*

My job is the history and the systems: what the ledger tracks, how the estates react, what the Electors want, what happens when you take Florentine money and don't march on Milan. I write that down as plainly as I can, Claude turns it into code, and I play it until something feels wrong.

The engine never knows who you are. Every campaign is a data entry: a ruler, a starting treasury, a court, rivals, ambitions, and its own historical events, tagged to the nations they belong to. Adding Frederick of Nuremberg as a third campaign was mostly writing history, not code.

\*\*Art: 90+ assets in one style\*\*

The illuminated-manuscript look comes from GPT image generation: knights, pikemen, trebuchets, castles, bishoprics, free cities, sea monsters, and portraits of almost 70 historical rulers. The hard part wasn't generating images, it was keeping them consistent. A small script cuts them out and converts them for the map.

The music is made by Funky Frank.

\*\*Playtesting in the open\*\*

Every version goes up as a free browser game on [sagaskald.com](http://sagaskald.com), and the code lives on GitHub so I can always roll back. Feedback from Reddit has shaped a lot, including some blunt opinions about the AI art, which is why the first Kickstarter stretch goal pays a human artist to redraw everything.

\*\*What I learned\*\* 

\- Small, concrete requests work better than "make it better".

\- Keep the history and the rules in plain text the AI can read. It's your real design document.

\- Play your own game every day. The AI can write the code; it can't tell you it's boring.

\*\*What's next\*\*

The full desktop edition with offline play, save slots and more content arrives on Steam in March 2027. €10, every core mechanic included, no DLC over €3.

[Free web edition](https://sagaskald.com/en/spel/rex-romanorum)



Happy to answer questions about any part of the workflow.



Oscar
